recipes.name: Black & White Malted Brownie Cookies
recipes.notes: Centers look underdone at 12 min and set as they cool. Test one sheet first: the vanilla half has no cocoa butter, so it may spread a little more — chill longer if it does.
recipes.method:
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line sheets with parchment
choc = melt together; cool slightly <- Chocolate, Bittersweet + Butter @dark
ribbonD = whip on high to a pale ribbon, 5 min <- Eggs @dark + Dark Brown Sugar @dark + Granulated Sugar @dark + Vanilla Extract @dark
batterD = fold in <- ribbonD + choc
dryD = whisk <- Flour @dark + Dutch-Process Cocoa Powder + Malted Milk Powder @dark + Espresso Powder + Baking Powder @dark + Salt @dark
darkDough = fold just until no streaks; chill 20 min <- batterD + dryD
melted = melt; cool slightly <- Butter @vanilla
ribbonV = whip on high to a pale ribbon, 5 min <- Eggs @vanilla + Dark Brown Sugar @vanilla + Granulated Sugar @vanilla + Vanilla Extract @vanilla
batterV = fold in <- ribbonV + melted
dryV = whisk <- Flour @vanilla + Malted Milk Powder @vanilla + Baking Powder @vanilla + Salt @vanilla
vanillaDough = fold just until no streaks; chill 20 min <- batterV + dryV
scoop ~1 Tbsp of each dough into one ball (24); bake 350°F 12–13 min until edges set; cool 5 min on sheet <- darkDough + vanillaDough

recipes.name: Coca-Cola Molasses Crinkle Cookies
recipes.notes: COLA SYRUP: Mexican Coke has ~110 g sugar per liter; reducing each liter to ~141 g (≈100 ml) matches molasses' ~22% water. Weigh the empty pot, simmer flat Coke in stainless or enameled (not aluminum/cast iron), and reduce until it weighs 141 g per liter started (2 L → ~282 g); it will bubble around 225°F near the end but trust the scale. Optional: a little lime zest or cola extract stirred into the cooled syrup for more cola aroma. If a test cookie tastes faintly soapy/metallic, cut baking soda to 8 g.
recipes.method:
prep: Reduce Coca-Cola to molasses strength — 141 g syrup per liter of Coke; cool (see notes)
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line sheets with parchment
base = whisk until smooth <- Vegetable Oil + Granulated Sugar @dough + Dark Brown Sugar
wet = whisk in <- base + Reduced Coca-Cola Syrup + Eggs + Vanilla Extract
dry = whisk <- Flour + Ground Ginger + Ground Cinnamon + Ground Cloves + Baking Soda
dough = fold just until no flour streaks <- wet + dry
balls = roll 1½ in. balls (~30 g); roll generously in sugar <- dough + Granulated Sugar @coating
bake 350°F 8–10 min until cracked with soft centers; cool 5 min on sheet <- balls

recipes.name: Cherry Phosphate Shortbread Thumbprints
recipes.book: Your Jam Thumbprint Cookies (flavor ideas from Art of Drink)
recipes.refrigerate: Chill shaped cookies while oven preheats
recipes.notes: PRESERVES: homemade from frozen pitted sour cherries or drained jarred Morellos; cook in a wide stainless pan (the fruit is acidic). WILD CHERRY SYRUP (Art of Drink, https://www.artofdrink.com/soda/cherry-phosphate) — full recipe makes 12 fl oz: 1 oz wild cherry bark, 1 fl oz glycerin, 4 fl oz water (first maceration), 4 fl oz warm water (second), 4 fl oz cherry juice, 10 oz sugar. One-third of the recipe covers 4 batches. ACID PHOSPHATE: the ⅔ tsp per batch keeps the drink's ratio (1 tsp per 1½ oz syrup) for traditional acid phosphate; with MacSweetie's, add drops to the cooled jam to taste and record the count. Built on your Jam Thumbprint proportions (yolk only, no added liquid, no baking soda) so the wells hold.
recipes.method:
prep: Day before: start the wild cherry syrup (see notes; make one batch for the whole plan)
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line sheets with parchment
extract = macerate 24 h; strain; re-steep bark in warm water 1 h; strain; combine <- Wild Cherry Bark + Vegetable Glycerin + Water
juiced = add; top up with water to volume <- extract + Tart Cherry Juice
syrup = dissolve without heat (use 2 Tbsp per batch) <- juiced + Granulated Sugar @syrup
preserves = cook, crushing some fruit, to 220°F or until a drop wrinkles on a cold plate, ~25–30 min <- Sour Cherries + Granulated Sugar @preserves + Lemon Juice
jam = stir in; simmer back to a thick jam; cool completely <- preserves + syrup
filling = stir in off heat, to taste <- jam + Acid Phosphate Solution
creamed = cream until fluffy, 2 min <- Butter + Granulated Sugar @dough + Honey
wet = beat in <- creamed + Egg Yolks + Cherry Extract + Almond Extract
dry = whisk <- Flour + Freeze-Dried Cherry Powder + Baking Powder + Salt
dough = mix on low just until combined <- wet + dry
shaped = roll 1 in. balls (~19 g), press wells; chill on sheets while oven heats <- dough
baked = fill ~½ tsp each; bake 350°F 12–13 min until edges just set; cool on sheet 5 min <- shaped + filling
dust when cool <- baked + Powdered Sugar

recipes.name: Egg Cream Pop Rock Wafer Sandwiches
recipes.book: Custom (wafer after King Arthur-style chocolate wafers)
recipes.notes: Wafers crisp further as they cool; if any center flexes once cool, return to the oven 2–3 min. The creme is water-free on purpose so the popping candy keeps its pop — keep the filled sandwiches airtight and assemble close to packing.
recipes.method:
prep: Heat oven to 325°F; line sheets with parchment
creamed = cream until fluffy, 2 min <- Butter + Granulated Sugar
wet = beat in until smooth <- creamed + Whole Milk + Vanilla Extract
dry = whisk <- Flour + Dutch-Process Cocoa Powder + Baking Soda + Salt @wafer
dough = mix on low just until a dough forms <- wet + dry
sheets = roll 1/16 in. between parchment; chill 30 min <- dough
wafers = cut 2 in. rounds (48), re-roll scraps; bake 325°F ~14 min until dry and fully crisp; cool completely <- sheets
base = beat until light and fluffy, 3 min <- Vegetable Shortening + Powdered Sugar + Nonfat Milk Powder + Vanilla Extract + Salt @creme
creme = fold in at the last minute <- base + Popping Candy (unflavored)
pipe ~13 g creme on 24 wafers, top with the rest, press gently; store airtight, 1–2 days before packing <- wafers + creme

recipes.name: Root Beer Float Millionaire's Bars
recipes.notes: Cream caramel, no condensed milk: use a 6 qt or larger pot, since the cream foams up as it boils. Temperature sets the texture: 240°F soft, 245°F chewy (cuts cleanly), 250°F firm. Keep the white-chocolate layer thin so it reads as vanilla ice cream rather than candy. Root beer caramel idea after Clever Pink Pirate (https://cleverpinkpirate.com/root-beer-caramel-recipe/). Bars are large (~70 g); cut 48 for cookie-box size.
recipes.method:
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line a 9×13 pan with a parchment sling
creamed = cream until light, 3 min <- Butter @crust + Granulated Sugar @crust + Dark Brown Sugar @crust
wet = beat in <- creamed + Egg Yolks + Vanilla Extract @crust
crumbs = mix on low until crumbly <- wet + Flour + Salt @crust
crust = press evenly into pan; bake 350°F 25 min until edges are golden; cool <- crumbs
cooked = bring to a boil, stirring; cook over medium, stirring often, to 245°F (firm ball) for a chewy set, 45–60 min <- Granulated Sugar @caramel + Dark Brown Sugar @caramel + Glucose + Heavy Cream + Butter @caramel + Salt @caramel
caramel = off heat, stir in <- cooked + Vanilla Extract + Sarsaparilla / Root Beer Extract + Ground Star Anise
layered = pour over crust; set until firm, ~2 h <- crust + caramel
melted = melt gently <- Chocolate, White + Vanilla Extract @top
spread ~2 mm thin over the caramel; sprinkle salt; set; cut 24 bars with a hot knife <- layered + melted + Flaky Sea Salt

recipes.name: Lime Rickey Drops
recipes.notes: Pull them while pale so they stay soft and cakey. The citric acid goes in the glaze (not sprinkled on top) so it doesn't weep in the mail. Optional: a tiny drop of green gel in the glaze.
recipes.method:
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line sheets with parchment
zested = rub together until fragrant <- Granulated Sugar + Lime Zest @dough
creamed = cream until fluffy, 2 min <- zested + Butter
wet = beat in; it may look curdled <- creamed + Eggs + Sour Cream + Lime Juice @dough + Vanilla Extract
dry = whisk <- Flour + Baking Powder + Baking Soda + Salt
dough = mix on low just until combined; chill 30 min <- wet + dry
cookies = scoop 2 Tbsp (~30 g); bake 350°F 9–11 min, just set and not browned; cool completely <- dough
glaze = whisk smooth <- Powdered Sugar + Lime Juice @glaze + Citric Acid
dip tops; finish with zest; set 30 min <- cookies + glaze + Lime Zest @glaze

notes.notes: Built on your proven Jam Thumbprint proportions (egg yolk only, no added liquid, no baking soda) so the wells hold. Cream butter, sugar and honey; beat in yolk and extracts; mix in flour, cherry powder, baking powder and salt. Roll 1 in. balls, press wells, chill shaped cookies while the oven preheats. WILD CHERRY SYRUP (Art of Drink, https://www.artofdrink.com/soda/cherry-phosphate): make it in one batch. The full recipe uses 1 oz bark, 1 fl oz glycerin, 4 fl oz water, a second 4 fl oz warm water, 4 fl oz cherry juice and 10 oz sugar, and makes 12 fl oz. Mix glycerin with the first 4 oz water, pour over the bark, macerate 24 h, then strain. Add the warm water to the bark for 1 h, strain, and combine. Add cherry juice, top up with water to 12 fl oz, and dissolve the sugar without heat. Each batch of cookies uses 2 Tbsp (1 fl oz) of syrup; 1/3 of the recipe covers 4 batches. FILLING per batch: simmer the preserves with 2 Tbsp syrup back to a thick jam, then cool. Off heat stir in 2/3 tsp acid phosphate, the drink ratio of 1 tsp per 1 1/2 oz syrup; add more to taste for extra tang. Fill about 1/2 tsp per cookie. Bake at 350°F for 12-13 min until edges just set. Dust with powdered sugar once cool. (Retro Soda Fountain 2026; base batch = 36.)

MOLASSES-STRENGTH COLA SYRUP: reduce Coca-Cola (Mexican, cane sugar) until it has about the same water content as molasses (~22%). Coke has 39 g sugar per 355 ml (~110 g per liter), so each liter reduces to about 141 g of syrup (~100 ml, a scant 1/2 cup). Method: weigh your empty pot, simmer flat Coke, and keep reducing until the contents weigh 141 g per liter you started with (2 L -> ~282 g). Near the end it will be bubbling around 225°F; trust the scale over the thermometer. Coke's phosphoric acid inverts some of the sugar as it cooks, which helps keep the syrup from crystallizing, like molasses. Swap it 1:1 by weight for molasses: 85 g (1/4 cup) per batch. Then whisk oil and sugars, add syrup, egg and vanilla, mix in dry, roll 1.5 in. balls in sugar, and bake at 350°F for 8-10 min. (Retro Soda Fountain 2026; base batch = 24.)
